items.title: Al Chez interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, February 13, 2019
items.q: I came back home and I called Shaffer up and I said, “I really don’t want to go on the road anymore,” You know Tom Malone was playing trumpet and trombone. Great trombone player. Trumpet owner. So I was like if you want to add a trumpet full time I won’t go on the road anymore.

ctx.x: They couldn’t find anybody good, yeah, yeah, yeah.

So then when they moved to CBS I was out on the West Coast playing with Tower of Power and the Robert Cray Band. And I did that for a while. I came back home and I called Shaffer up and I said, “I really don’t want to go on the road anymore,” You know Tom Malone was playing trumpet and trombone. Great trombone player. Trumpet owner. items.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023
items.q: I don’t know if Chez was with us on that day or not anymore

ctx.x: Oh yeah, yeah, yeah, she mentioned it. She says, “I’ve got a tape of you singing those ten songs in full voice whatever that means. To me it was just really a day’s work but then Tom was able to take my tape and arrange it and he did a beautiful job and we brought in special — you know he asked for a bassoon I think and an oboe. New York is the kind of

place where you just make one call and they’re there at 10 AM. Renee Fleming came into my dressing room, we had our little woodwind ensemble Chez — I don’t know if Chez was with us on that day or not anymore, but parts for everybody thanks to Tom, who stayed up all night writing these things, and then Renee making sure that she could time them right. Because it’s got to be camera goes back to Dave, he says, “Number seven” bang back to Renee who is now singing it. So really when he’s saying “Number seven” I’m…
